action: Execute the formal site visit and property valuation for Amir Patel. He called back. He accepted the offer. I go to the Route 9 station this week with a property assessment form, comp data, and a pre-prepared scenario framework. I deliver two things in writing: (1) Current market value as-is — my estimate in this market, accounting for the spending index at 42, the auto row distressed designation, and the thinning buyer pool, is $285,000–$330,000 for his parcel, which has utility infrastructure and highway visibility that provides a floor other auto row parcels do not have. That number is lower than it would have been at tick 4 and it will be lower again at tick 10 if employment does not recover. I tell him that directly. (2) A comparative scenario analysis across four paths: fuel-only continued operation (revenue trajectory under continued spending compression, customer base exposed to workforce contraction), EV charging retrofit (infrastructure conversion cost estimate, demand timeline based on RoboRide fleet expansion, net present value comparison), full adaptive reuse sale to a third party buyer (current comp range, likely buyer profiles — delivery logistics operators are now a real category given today's announcement, EV fleet services, light industrial conversion), and hybrid lease arrangement (retain ownership, find an operator tenant who converts the site while Amir draws a lease income). I spend two hours on the site, pull his financials from the conversation if he is willing to share them, and leave him with a one-page written summary he can use with his accountant, his family, and any buyer who comes to him directly. The valuation fee will be settled in a subsequent tick once the scope is confirmed — I do not make this about money today. I make it about him having the complete picture.
